errors.text_span: with major gridlines at 5, 10, and 15 percentage point intervals
errors.evidence: The y-axis gridlines are at a constant interval of 5 percentage points (at 40, 45, 50, 55, 60, 65), not at varying intervals of 5, 10, and 15.
The plot displays six distinct methods, as shown in the legend (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, ROME), not five.
The plot and legend show that the marker for MEMIT is a purple pentagon, not a purple square. The square marker belongs to the ROME series.
The starting accuracy for the "Base" method is clearly below 40% on the y-axis, approximately at 38%. The stated value of 41% is incorrect.
The description omits the "IKE" method (red line with triangle markers) entirely from its list of methods.

The marker for the FT series is an inverted triangle. The description's use of "triangles" is imprecise and potentially confusing, as the IKE series (which was omitted) uses standard triangle markers.
The starting point for the ROME method is just above 50%, closer to 51%. The value 52% is a slight over-approximation.
